chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was circumambulating the Kaaba when I saw a man saying, 'What is the matter with these two corners that they are kissed, while these two are not?' So I said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) kissed these two and did not face/present to these two, so do not present to them, since the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not present to them.'
Jamil said: And I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) kissing all the corners. And it is recommended to kiss all the corners.

key_terms.اَلرُّكْنَانِ: The two corners (specifically referring to the Yamani and the Corner)
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: It is recommended (a fiqh term for a recommended act)

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory or recommended to kiss all four corners of the Kaaba during pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the Prophet’s specific Sunnah of kissing the Yamani and Eastern corners and the general recommendation for the faithful to kiss all four corners, as observed by Imam al-Sadiq. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on emulating the Prophet’s unique practices while adhering to broader ritual recommendations, reinforcing the Kaaba’s role as a focal point of devotion. The hadith also illustrates the methodological principle of reconciling specific prophetic actions with general communal practices in Islamic law.
